questions.question: When did the Non-Cooperation Movement end?
questions.solution:
The Non-Cooperation Movement which was launched by Mahatma Gandhi in 1920 Continued till **__1922__**.

 
• The Non-Cooperation Movement was initiated by Mahatma Gandhi with the aim of self- governance and against the Rowlatt Act and the Jallianwala Bagh Massacre.
 
• The Non-Cooperation Movement Ended in 1922 after the Chauri-Chaura incident in Gorakhpur where a large group of protesters, participating in the Non-cooperation movement, clashed with police, who opened fire.
 
• A similar type of movement was initiated in 1930 as Civil Disobedience movement named as Namak Satyagraha Aandolan.

questions.question: ‘Dhansiri’ is a tributary of which of the following river?
questions.solution:
Dhansiri is a tributary of the __**Bramhaputra**__ River.

 
• Dhansiri originates from the Laisang peak of Nagaland and flows through the Golaghat District of Assam and the Dimapur District of Nagaland and finally joins the Brahmaputra river at Dhansirimukh.
 
• The Brahmputra river originates from the Mansarovar Lake Region near Mount Kailash and flows through China, India, and Bangladesh and joins Padma(Ganges) in Bangladesh.
 
• The world's largest river island lies in the Brahmputra river named as "Majuli" as recorded in the Guinness Book of World Records and it is the first river Island in India.

questions.question: ‘Equus caballus’ is the scientiﬁc name of which of the following animals?
questions.solution:
Equus Ferus Caballus is the Scientific name of __**Horse**__ which is most prominent among the domesticated animals since 3500 BC.

 
• Horses are bred and used for warfare since 3000 BC in the Bronze Age.
 
• The Horses belong to Mammalia class Chordata Phylum in the Animalia Kingdom.
 
• The largest horse in recorded history was probably a Shire horse named Mammoth, who was born in 1848. He stood 21.2 1⁄4 hands (86.25 inches, 219 cm) high and his peak weight was estimated at 1,524 kilograms.
 
• The current record holder for the world's smallest horse is Thumbelina, a fully mature miniature horse affected by dwarfism. She is 17 in (43 cm) tall and weighs 26 kg.

questions.question: Which of the following state of India is main producer of Chromite?
questions.solution:
**__Odisha__** is the largest and almost the sole producer of Chromite in India.

 
• Chromite is the only economic ore of chromium which is an oxide of iron and chromium which is used in chrome plating and alloying for the production of various materials such as corrosion-resistant superalloys, nichrome, and stainless steel etc.
 
• Goa as a state is not only important for tourism but it is also endowed with Mineral Resources like Iron ore, Manganese ore, Bauxite and other minor minerals too.
 
• Rajasthan is the State of Great Thar desert yet it is the producer of minerals such as Zinc, Gypsum, Silver and many more.
 
• Haryana's Land is rich in minerals like Gold, Copper, Garnet, Calcite, Beryl, Baryte, Graphite, Dolomite and various others too.

questions.question: Which of the following ions are responsible for hardness of water?
questions.solution:
The ions of **__Calcium and Magnesium__** are responsible for the hardness of water where the concentration of certain minerals is what creates the “hardness” of water.

 
• The hardness of water is developed due to the sufficiency of carbonates and Bi-Carbonates of Calcium and Magnesium.
 
• There are no serious adverse health problems associated with drinking hard water But, hard water can contribute to dry skin and hair.
 
• Generally, the hardness of water is measured by the means of TDS meter which measures the hardness on the basis of Electrical Conductivity of the Water.

questions.solution:

questions.question: Who was the Mughal emperor during the 1857 revolt in India?
questions.solution:
The Mughal Emperor during the 1857 revolt in India was __**Bahadur Shah II**__ (Bahadur Shah Zafar) who was the 19th and the last Mughal Emperor.

 
• The 1857 revolt was a very major rebellion against the rule of the British East India Company, which functioned as a sovereign power on behalf of the British Crown.
 
• The Revolt of 1857 or the Indian Mutiny was originated due to the British policy of expansion through the Doctrine of Lapse and direct annexation.
 
• Alamgir II was the 14th Emperor of the Mughal dynasty who ruled between 1754 to 1759 and he was succeeded by Shah Jahan III.
 
• Akbar Shah II was the predecessor of Bahadur Shah Zafar and he was the 18th Emperor of the Mughal dynasty who ruled between 1806 to 1837.
 
• Shah Alam II was the 16th Mughal Emperor who ruled between 1760 & 1806.

questions.question: Which of the following is the traditional theatre of Jammu and Kashmir?
questions.solution:
__**Bhand Pather**__ is the traditional theatre of Jammu & Kashmir which consists of the unique combinations of Dance, Drama & Acting.

 
• The word 'Bhand' is used to represent the traditional folk entertainers of India, Bangladesh & Nepal and the people, as well as their presentation materials, differ from region to region.
 
• Bhand Pather of the Jammu & Kashmir perform to commemorate the lives of rishis(Sufi Sages, both Hindus, and Muslims) or more contemporary real or fictional figures are enacted by them.
 
• Maach is the traditional theatre that belongs to Rajasthan and Madhya Pradesh along with Jatra and Swaang of Bengal and Haryana respectively.

questions.question: Which of the following is a Communicable disease?
questions.solution:
__**Concept**__

__**Measles**__ is a communicable disease among the options provided in the question.

__
 
• Measles is a highly contagious disease that is caused due to the Measles Virus in which the Symptoms include fever, cough, runny nose and inflamed eyes.
 
• Measles can spread through direct contact with the mouth or nasal secretions as well as by coughs and sneezes of infected people due to which it is also an Airborne Disease.
 
• The measles vaccine was first introduced in 1985 when it was imported to India but India became self-sufficient since 1991 and its introduction in the society led to an 80% decrease in deaths due to Measles.
 
• Measles Vaccine was discovered by Maurice Hilleman who was an American microbiologist who was specialized in vaccinology. In addition to Measles, Maurice Hilleman has also developed the vaccines for mumps, hepatitis A, hepatitis B, chickenpox, meningitis, pneumonia, and Haemophilus Influenzae bacteria.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e085a7f17645c801966c030eb44d69fae944b96fdb4c4077f5fba1bc2c24bc71.png] **Mistake Points__**

 
• Asthma is a major non-communicable disease, affecting both children and adults, and is the most common chronic disease among children.
 
• Inflammation and narrowing of the small airways in the lungs cause asthma symptoms, which can be any combination of cough, wheeze, shortness of breath and chest tightness.

questions.question: ‘Kajri’ folk song is related to which of the following state?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** __Uttar Pradesh.__**

__
 
• Kajri Folk Song is related to India's largest state **Uttar Pradesh **__as well as Bihar.
 
• Kajri folk song is often used to describe the longing of a maiden for her lover as the black monsoon cloud arrives in the summer skies, and the style is notably sung during the rainy season.
 
• Kajri folk song is traditionally sung in the villages and towns of Uttar Pradesh around Banaras, Mirzapur, Mathura, Allahabad, and the Bhojpur regions of Bihar.
 
• Maand Folk Song is the traditional folk song of Rajasthan whereas Koli and Lavani Folk Songs belong to Maharashtra and Himachal Pradesh is enriched with the great folk song Jhoori.

questions.question: According to the Census 2011,what is the literacy rate of India?
questions.solution:
According to the census 2011, the literacy rate of India is mentioned as __**0.7404**__ i.e- 74.04%.

 
• Among the total literates in India, there are 33,42,50,358 females and 44,42,03,762 are males i.e- 65.5% and 82.1% respectively.
 
• In the case of literacy rates Kerala, Mizoram & Lakshadweep hold the first, second & third positions respectively.
 
• Any person who is aged seven years and above and who can both read and write in any language is treated as ‘literate’ and It is not necessary that a person should receive any formal education or pass any minimum education standard.
 
• Literacy can also be achieved in adult literacy classes or through any non-formal education system.
 
• People who are blind but can read in braille are also treated as literates.

questions.question: Who is the writer of the book ‘Thoughts on Pakistan’?
questions.solution:
The Book "Thoughts of Pakistan" was authored by **__Dr B R Ambedkar__** who was the First Law Minister of the in independent India.

 
• Dr. B R Ambedkar was a well-renowned Politician, Jurist and Social reformer who promoted to revolt against Social discrimination and untouchability.
 
• Dr. B R Ambedkar is Known as the "Father of Indian Constitution" because he was the member of the constituent assembly and the Chairman of the Drafting Committee of the Indian Constitution.
 
• Dr. B R Ambedkar was a renowned Jurist, economist, politician, social reformer as well as he was posthumously awarded the highest civilian award Bharat Ratna in 1990.

questions.question: The concept of ‘The Four Noble Truths’ belongs to which of the following religions?
questions.solution:
The concept of "the Four Noble Truths" belongs to __**Buddhism**__.

 
• Buddhism was established by "Buddha" approximately 2500 years ago in India and it is 4th largest religion with approximate
ly 7% of the world's population.
 
• Gautam Buddha was born in Lumbini in Nepal to the King of Kapilvastu but he left his palace at the age of 29 which is known as Mahabhinishkramana.
 
• The Four Noble Truths of Buddism is-
 
 
• Dukkha(The truth of Suffering)
 
• Samudaya(To find the cause of suffering)
 
• Nirodh(To find the cessation of suffering)
 
• Magga(Implementation of the right path to end suffering)
 
 
 
• The Buddhism was categorised initially in two sects namely, Hinayana & Mahayana but in the later era, Various sects of Neo-Buddhism also originated and among these, the most promoted & accepted form is Navayana which was launched by Dr Bhimrao Ambedkar.

questions.question: Which of the following Vitamin is related to Osteoporosis?
questions.solution:
__**Vitamin-D**__ which is a fat-soluble vitamin is closely related to Osteoporosis.

 
• Osteoporosis is a disease related to the bone, in which bones lose their density due to which the bones weaken and become prone to breakage.
 
• The deficiency of Vitamin-D can be compensated by the intake of cod liver oils, cheese, egg yolks, and mushrooms as well as body also absorbs it from exposure to Sunlight.
 
• The deficiency of Vitamin-A leads a person to Nightblindness & Xeropthalmia which is common in Africa and South-Asia and this deficiency could be fulfilled by the intake of the Beef liver, Spinach, Black-eyed pea, Brocol
li, and various others.
 
• The deficiency of Vitamin-B causes Beri-Beri and this deficiency could be fulfilled by the intake of meat, fish, whole grains, nuts, cereals, and others.
 
• The deficiency of Vitamin-C causes Scurvy and this deficiency could be fulfilled by the intake of citrus fruits like kiwi, orange, lemon, guava as well as broccoli, and cauliflower.

questions.question: Which of the following Articles is related to Jammu & Kashmir?
questions.solution:
Article 370 was related to the Jammu & Kashmir which has been partially reprimanded in recent days to withdraw the special status to the State of Jammu & Kashmir.

 
• President Ram Nath Kovind issued a constitutional order on 5th August 2019 which superseded the Presidential order of 1954 making all the provisions of the Indian constitution applicable to Jammu and Kashmir.
 
• Following this Presidential order of 2019, another resolution was passed in both houses of the Parliament leading to the issuance of another order on 6th August 2019 declaring all the clauses of Article 370 except clause 1 to be inoperative.
 
• In the light of Presidential Orders of 2019, Jammu & Kashmir Reorganisation Act was passed by both the Houses of Parliament which enacted the division of State of Jammu & Kashmir into two union territories i.e- Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh on 31st October 2019.

questions.question: Who among the following has the power to promulgate ordinance?
questions.solution:
The First-person of the country, "__President__" has the Power to Promulgate Ordinance.

 
• Article 123 of the Constitution of India gives the right to President of India to Promulgate Ordinance in India on the recommendation of Union Cabinet.
 
• This right to the President can be exercised only in the case when either of the two Houses of Parliament is not in session to enact laws. 
 
• Article 213 of the constitution of India provides the power to the Governor of States to promulgate Ordinance.
 
• The Ordinance can be promulgated by the President of India for 6 weeks and it must be approved by Parliament within six weeks of reassembling or they shall cease to operate.
